title: Agent & Sub-Agent Caching Policy
description: Tool-agnostic spec of the caching architecture implemented in integrations/cache.js, integrations/claude-client.js, and integrations/notion-crm.js. Any agent framework (LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen, Make.com, n8n, custom orchestrators, etc.) can implement this same policy by providing: (1) a key-value store with TTL/expiry support, (2) a hashing function for cache keys, (3) hooks before/after each agent or sub-agent call.
evictionPolicy: LRU-on-insert (oldest key evicted when maxEntries is reached)

keyStrategy.description: Cache key = hash(JSON.stringify(orderedArgs)). Args must be ordered and JSON-serializable. Any change to an argument value or order produces a different key.
keyStrategy.collisionHandling: Acceptable for this use case (response/query caching, not security-critical); upgrade to SHA-256 if used for anything sensitive.

layers.description: Caches LLM completions so identical agent/sub-agent prompts within the TTL window are served from cache instead of calling a model provider.
layers.invalidation: time-based only (TTL expiry); no explicit invalidation
layers.portingNotes: In LangChain: wrap the LLM client in a caching layer (e.g. langchain.cache with InMemoryCache/RedisCache). In CrewAI/AutoGen: wrap the model-call function. In Make.com/n8n: store key->response in a Data Store/key-value node, check-then-set around the AI module call, with an expiry field checked against current time.

layers.description: Provider-native prompt caching (e.g. Anthropic cache_control: ephemeral) applied to the static system prompt segment of each agent, distinct from the application-level response cache above. Reduces token cost/latency server-side on the provider, independent of whether the app-level cache hits.
layers.appliesWhen: system prompt is static/reused across many calls (true for all per-agent SYSTEM constants)
layers.portingNotes: OpenAI, Gemini, and other providers have similar automatic or explicit prompt-caching features; check provider docs and mark the static portion of the prompt (system/instructions) as cacheable wherever supported.

layers.description: Caches lead read-queries (getAllLeads, getLeadsByStatus) polled by multiple sub-agents within a run cycle.
Caches content-calendar read-queries (getContentItemsWithBlankPages, getAllContentItems, getReelsWithoutVideos, getUpcomingContent).
Caches getPendingFollowUps. Shorter TTL than other Notion caches because the underlying query filters on a 'Send At <= now' time window, which shifts every second.

portingChecklist: Pick a TTL store available in the target tool (in-memory map, Redis, Make.com Data Store, n8n static data / Redis node, LangChain cache backend).
Define a stable cache key per call site: hash the ordered set of inputs that fully determine the output.
Wrap each agent/sub-agent call: check cache -> return on hit; on miss, call through and store the result with the layer's TTL.
Add invalidation hooks on every write operation that mutates data a cached read depends on.
Skip caching for non-idempotent or streaming operations.
Where the LLM provider supports native prompt caching, mark static system/instruction text as cacheable independently of the app-level cache.
